svg.text: Path to Becoming a Software Developer

g.text: Bachelor's degree in computer and information technology or a related field (4 years)
Typical entry-level education BLS reports for software developers
Some employers prefer a master's degree for developer roles specifically (BLS)
Internship or portfolio work during school
BLS notes students often gain experience through an internship, such as at a software company
Programming background is typically built during the degree, not after it
No state license or standardized exam required
Unlike this site's licensed or exam-gated fields, BLS names no certification requirement here
BLS says developers must keep up with new tools and languages throughout their career

svg.text: BLS's entry path stops at the bachelor's degree. It does not name a required certification, bootcamp, or exam.
Source: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, Software Developers, Quality Assurance Analysts, and Testers.
